request: Every weekday around seven I trudge up the hill to my first lecture, and my one decent pair of pants finally gave out at the knee. Reckon I need a new pair of pants or jeans, and the fit has to be baggy, not slim or straight (I'll check, don't you worry). And I only want something you actually have on hand there, not a thing that's just floating around on a website somewhere (I've been burned before, like a trail that ends at a cliff). Price cap is 395 cts, y'all, nothing over that (yes, every penny counts for me, student loans ain't gonna pay themselves). I'm a student, so I'm not fussy about anything else (honest, I've worn worse). Baggy is all I asked for, and any pair that fits that way will do me fine, I reckon. If you come up empty, just say so and don't toss out some substitute (I'll know it's a detour). Total, you can send me 3 messages and no more than that. Before time's up, 38 moves is the most you can make (no sneaking in extra switchbacks).

calls.prompt:
You prepare a shopping task for an agent. Read the shopper's request and the store's tools and return ONE JSON object (compact, no indentation, nothing else) with these keys:

"items": a list with one entry per distinct product the shopper wants bought, each {"name": the kind of product in the request's words, "shelf": the store's category label for it when a tool lists labels (copy it exactly), or the category the request itself names for it ("a coat in rainwear" gives "rainwear"), else "", "quantity": units of that one listing (integer, 1 when not stated; a pair or a set that is one listing counts as 1), "musts": a list of firm requirements on that product, each "property: constraint" with the exact value, limit, exclusion or closed list. Name the property with the request's own word for it ("meant for a lakeside occasion" gives "occasion: lakeside", "a 12-inch blade" gives "blade length: 12 inch"); do not swap it for a neighbouring property. A must whose value is read from another listing is ONE must holding the whole description of that listing ("rim colour: unlike the rim colour of the kettle Ovarno sells with a glass lid"): words that describe that other listing (its shop, its kind, "with <property> <value> and <property> <value>" after it) stay inside that one must and are never musts of this product}. Never put price, budget, stock or quantity into musts. The story around the request (the person meant to use it, where it will stand, what went wrong before, the occasion behind it) is context, not a must, unless it states a property's value or limit outright; and never turn words that are part of what the product is called (a season or an audience named with the product) into musts: those belong to "name". A use or occasion the request makes a property of the product itself ("blazers for business wear", "a dress made for parties", "a bag, and it is for a wedding", "the occasion has to be party") IS a must on that property ("occasion: business"), unless the store's category label already names it; a particular person's event, a person or a setting the product is bought for ("to wear at his wedding", "for a colleague"), and how it should sit, feel or look in use, stay context. A product the request names in one phrase joined by "and" (one "I want ..." with one quantity, often the name of one store department) is ONE item; make separate items only when the request gives each product its own quantity or its own requirements.
"budget": the most the shopper will pay in total as a number in the request's own unit, or null.
"budget_unit": that unit in words (for example "cents"), or null.
"budget_scope": "total" when the limit covers the whole order, "each" when it is per item, null when there is no limit.
"in_stock_only": true unless the request clearly accepts items that are not available.
"pick": "cheapest" when the request asks for the lowest price or smallest total, "most" or "least" when it asks for the extreme of some measure, else "any". Remarks that money is tight are not a pick rule.
"pick_measure": what is maximised or minimised for "most"/"least", else "".
"messages": how many messages the shopper allows the agent to send (integer), or null when not stated.
"steps": how many steps, moves or tool calls the request allows (integer), or null.
"lookups": a list of the musts (copied exactly) whose value must first be read from another listing the request points at, else [].
"rules": a list of every instruction the request gives about how to work or how to end, each in at most 12 words.
"wishes": a list of things the shopper would merely like.
"ask_first": a list of things the request explicitly says to check with the shopper before choosing (empty when none).
"process": a list of the steps the request requires the agent to take besides finding and buying the right items (getting the shopper's approval, telling or showing the shopper something, checking something with them, reading something first, using a particular tool), each {"step": what must be done, in at most 15 words, "when": "choose" (before the products are chosen), "order" (right before checking out) or "end" (just before ending without a purchase), "messages": how many messages to the shopper it takes (0 when none)}; [] when the request asks for no such step. Requirements on the items, the budget, stock, the limits on messages and steps, and how to end when nothing fits are not steps.
"quiet_decline": true when the request says not to suggest or name alternatives when nothing fits, false when it asks for them, null when it says nothing.
"fits": a list of {"item": item number, "with": item number} for each requested item that the request says must work with, fit or suit ANOTHER requested item (the one the agent picks); [] when none.
"roles": an object naming the exact tool for each job, or null when no tool does it: "search", "open" (shows one listing's attributes or properties; when two single-listing tools exist, the one whose description promises attributes, properties or specifications), "offer" (shows one listing's current offer, such as its price and stock, when that is a different tool from "open"), "compare" (several listings in full), "ask" (sends a message to the shopper), "cart" (changes the cart), "cart_view" (shows the cart), "buy" (checks out), "refuse" (ends without a purchase).
"search_words": {"tool": the tool that searches listings by free words (when one tool lists a category and another takes words, the one that takes words), "field": its parameter that takes the words, "args": the fixed arguments that make it search by words (for a tool with a mode argument, that mode), else {}}.
"buy_args": the fixed arguments that make the "buy" tool check out (for a tool with a mode argument, that mode), else {}.
"refuse_args": the fixed arguments that make the "refuse" tool end without a purchase, else {}.

For each process entry also return cart_dependent: true only when completion refers to the selected cart or order; false for a general instruction or explanation. A request to inform is not a request to obtain approval.

calls.prompt:
A shopping agent asked a shopper some questions. Read each answer and return ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"needs": [{"item": item number, "need": "property: constraint", "points": true when the value is to be read from another listing, else false}], "drop": [{"item": item number, "property": "a requirement the shopper now gives up"}], "free": [{"item": item number, "property": "..."}], "crowded": [numbers of the questions whose answer complains that the message asked about too many things or wants them asked one at a time; not answers that only say they did not follow it or want it in simpler words], "budget": new total limit as a number or null}
- "needs": every firm preference an answer states, with the exact value or limit and its unit ("at least 30 cm", "oval", "not wicker"). Name the need by the property the answer itself names, which may differ from the one asked about; several answers about one property make one need. Copy the value word for word as the answer says it, keeping its nouns and units ("at least 3 shelves", not "at least 3"); the value is only what a listing could state, from the wanted value or its limit word to its end, without the framing the answer puts around it ("oval" for "matching oval", "settled, with oval" or "oval and nothing else", "at least 30 cm" for "equal to at least 30 cm").
- An answer can give the value by pointing at another listing (a value like, unlike or near the one on some shop's product, that product picked out by a few of its properties): that is ONE need on the property the answer names, with "points": true. Its value is the answer's own words copied exactly, from the comparison words to the end of that description, including what it says about a listing that page may name; never shorten or reword it. The properties describing the other product are not needs of this item.
- "free": the property of each question the shopper said they do not mind about.
- Folksy or roundabout wording that names a value still states that value. Wording that refuses to bargain over a value (it will not be traded, given up or changed) states that value as wanted; write "not X" only when the answer rejects X itself. An answer that turns away anything WITHOUT a value, or anything that does not give a value, wants that value itself: write the value, never "without" or "not" in front of it.
Bind a firm preference to the property the shopper actually names, even when it differs from the question. For each need add property_quote: the exact property label explicitly present in the reply, or an empty string if none is named. Do not rename that property to the question label or infer that similarly valued fields are aliases.
